chapter_title: Concerning the Interpretation of the Five Words that are proclaimed in the Universe
chapter_note: This chapter contains NO oldest teaching substrate. It is entirely a later editorial composition concerned with mapping terminology from contemporary sects (Baptists, Purified Ones/Catharioi, Mandaean 'First Life'/'Second Life') onto Manichaean divinities. The chapter is heavily damaged with extensive lacunae, only 3 short paragraphs survive. Teaching purity is 0.000 — no substrate vocabulary detected. The mapping here is tradition→tradition (sect term → Manichaean name), not cosmos→cosmos. Gardner confirms the chapter addresses contemporary sectarian identifications. This is editorial bridge material throughout, framed in dialogue format.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic disciple question ('Once again the disciples [questioned the apostle. They say to] him: Recount to us, our master') wrapping a question about contemporary sectarian terms. The question content — 'the sect of the Baptists', 'other sects', 'Purified Ones', 'First Life', 'Second Life' — references specific contemporary religious groups and their terminology. This is NOT a substantive cosmological question ('Tell us about the five storehouses'); it asks about terms used by identifiable sects. The entire paragraph is dialogue frame + institutional sectarian reference. No cosmic-to-cosmic mapping present.

Very fragmentary. 'Call it by this name is the Father, the life... this unnameable, whom no one [...] his name.' This equates a sectarian term (from the five words) with a Manichaean divine figure. The function is cross-traditional identification — one side of the mapping is a sect's term, the other is a Manichaean name. No correspondential structure (face, body, metal, taste) is present. The description 'this unnameable' is a theological epithet, not a cosmic-correspondential mapping. Editorial bridge: connecting external religious vocabulary to Manichaean theology.

Continues the enumeration: 'The second [word is the Thir]d Ambassador [...] whom they also call the father of [...] the first Father.' The formula 'whom they also call' is an explicit cross-traditional identification marker — mapping one tradition's name onto another's. 'The Third Ambassador' is a standard Manichaean divine name, not a substrate cosmological description. The paragraph performs inter-sectarian translation, not cosmic domain mapping. Very fragmentary — extensive lacunae make full assessment difficult, but what survives is consistently editorial bridge.
